item.title: Kokusai-dori Guide: Shopping, Eats & Access (Naha)
item.description: Kokusai-dori (“International Street”) is Naha’s bustling main thoroughfare — a roughly 1.6 km stretch lined with souvenir shops, restaurants, izakaya, cafés and street performers. Rebuilt in the years after WWII and nicknamed the “Miracle Mile,” it’s the liveliest place in Okinawa to shop for local crafts and snacks, sample Okinawan cuisine, and feel the island’s easygoing energy. Dip into the covered market arcades just off the main drag for a more local, atmospheric experience.

item.title: Shuri Castle Guide: Tickets, Reconstruction & Access (Naha)
item.description: Shuri Castle (Shurijō) was the political and ceremonial heart of the Ryukyu Kingdom for some 450 years, and remains Okinawa’s most important historic site. With its distinctive vermilion halls, Chinese- and Japanese-influenced architecture, and hilltop views over Naha, it is a UNESCO World Heritage component (“Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu”). A devastating fire in October 2019 destroyed the main hall (Seiden) and several structures; the castle is now in the midst of a multi-year reconstruction, which has itself become a fascinating thing to witness.

item.title: Yachimun Pottery Guide: Tsuboya Street & Workshops (Naha)
item.description: Yachimun is the Okinawan word for pottery, and the island’s bold, earthy ceramics are among its most beloved crafts. The heart of the tradition is Tsuboya, a historic pottery quarter just off Kokusai-dori in Naha, where a charming stone-paved lane is lined with kilns, studios, galleries and shops. Here you’ll find rustic plates and cups, awamori flasks, and the famous shisa lion-dog guardians. Browsing the lane — or trying the wheel yourself — is a lovely, low-key cultural break in the city.

item.title: Best Hotels & Ryokan in Okinawa: Naha, Onna Village & Island Resorts
item.description: Okinawa is Japan’s tropical paradise — a chain of 160 subtropical islands stretching 1,000 km from Kyushu to Taiwan. The main island (Okinawa Honto) has Japan’s best beach resort infrastructure; the outlying islands (Miyako, Ishigaki, Iriomote) offer world-class diving, largely undeveloped beaches, and a distinctly different culture from mainland Japan. Best Areas to Stay Onna Village / Motobu — Main Island Beach Resorts The central Pacific coast of the main island, from Motobu (near the Churaumi Aquarium) down through Onna Village.
